channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Integration: Genesis from Synthesis · Gather Center
item.description: Gather Center is a 501(c)3 arts and education nonprofit in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, founded in 2023 by Allison Harrell Mistier and André-Philippe Mistier and opened to the public in 2025 with a gallery, digital immersion spaces and a garden. Its programme runs on an annual “Consciousness Spiral” — Awakening in spring, Resonance in summer, Integration in autumn, Embodiment in winter — and this is Phase III. The call asks for work on Integration as “a movement of dynamic stillness, metabolism and revealing interconnections”, which the centre glosses with its own meditations: “The leaf nourishes the seed”, “Through the cracks came the light”, “Slow down to receive”. The framing is openly esoteric — “becoming borderless”, “point of permeability”, transmutation — and the gallery is explicit that it wants interconnection made visible rather than a literal illustration of the theme. Eligibility is open to all artists 18 and over with no location restriction, and the accepted-media list names photography alongside painting, works on paper, textile, sculpture, sound, music, multimedia and performance. One $35 fee covers up to three works. Wall works may run to 60 inches on any side and 40 pounds, projecting no more than six inches, and must arrive ready to hang on wire, D-rings or a cleat — no Velcro, adhesive strips, sawtooth hangers or tape; works on paper must be framed or glazed. The practical gate is physical, not geographic: selected work must be hand delivered to and collected from 94 Guernsey St in person, with drop-off on 18 November 2026 and pickup on 8 January 2027, so shipping is not an option. Notifications go out by 13 November, installation is 19 November, the opening reception is Friday 20 November 2026, 5.30–8.30 PM, and the show stays up through early January 2027, open Saturdays 12–5 PM. Selected audio may also join a companion online release, as the centre did with Resonance. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Man or Bear: No Safe Choice · Woman Made Gallery
item.description: Woman Made Gallery takes the viral question — alone in the woods, would you rather meet a man or a bear — and builds a spring exhibition out of what it exposed. The call is explicit about its subject: “male violence and abuse against women” as it is organised and amplified online, from “the undercurrents of red-pilling young boys and online stalking” to “AI-produced revenge porn, the trans-vestigation of female athletes, manosphere gaming culture, and disinformation smear campaigns of women in positions of power”. Its closing line sets the tone of what the gallery wants: “Both are wild, but at least a woman will be believed when she is attacked by a bear.” The published areas of inquiry are deliberately wide — critique of the manosphere, incel culture, online gender investigations targeting trans people, frat and rape culture, “reclamation of authorship, narrative power, and cultural agency”, intersectional experience across gender, race, class, sexuality, disability and migration, and art as a site of resistance — and the gallery asks for “your most raw reactions over a plethora of mediums and forms”. Submissions are open to women and nonbinary artists at all career stages “working in any medium”; stills and moving image are both accepted at upload. Selection is by MA students from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago rather than a single named juror. Entry is $30 for one to three works, with up to two entries per artist, and WMG publishes reduced fees and fee waivers reserved for BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ artists on request. Work previously shown at WMG is not eligible, nothing may exceed 6 feet on its widest side or 75 pounds unless the artist handles delivery and pickup personally, artists arrange and pay for shipping to the gallery, and sales carry a 40% commission. — Deadline: January 23, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: International Residency of Experimentation 2027 · Experimental Photo Festival
item.description: Six artists from different parts of the world come to Barcelona for eight intensive days of experimentation, shared learning and hands-on work in the week before Experimental Photo Festival 2027. The structure is horizontal rather than taught: each resident shares an experimental process with the group through one theoretical and practical session — two hours of theory, four of practice — and takes part in the sessions proposed by the other five, so knowledge moves from one artist to another, one cultural perspective to another and one process to the next. The residency is conducted in English so that all six can work in a common language, and it is aimed at artists willing to share what they know and curious about other people's practices. Residents stay at the Col·legi Major Penyafort-Montserrat and work across the residency spaces and the Centre Cívic Pati Llimona. During the festival itself, a collective exhibition presenting the process developed in the residency opens at Pati Llimona alongside a Residency Conference where the residents discuss what they worked on. APPLYING IS FREE, BUT A SELECTED PARTICIPANT PAYS €500, and the festival publishes the breakdown: accommodation €330, materials €30, bank and platform fees €30, and 21% tax €110, with payment possible in monthly instalments; the Association says it pays the residency director's salary from a public grant. That €500 covers the eight nights with breakfast, the materials for the workshops and collective experimentation, access to Experimental Photo Festival 2027, participation in the residency talk and exhibition, official festival merchandise, and a free place on the Diploma in Experimental Photography at Ágora, School of Experimentation, which the festival values at €999. It does not cover accommodation during the festival days, meals other than breakfast, travel or personal expenses. Continuing through the festival is optional and encouraged: a resident who adapts their residency workshop into a four-hour festival format can attend two workshops of their choice free, has their workshop materials provided, and gets meals on the days they work as a festival artist. Applications are reviewed by the Experimentalphotofestival Association together with residency coordinator Célica Véliz — a visual artist and photographer trained in photography, visual arts and ceramics, professor of Photochemical Processes I and II in the University Photography Programme at the National University of La Plata, and director of this residency since 2023 — and consider each artist's proposed practice and process and their ability to share it. An application is a biography of 250 to 500 words, a PDF portfolio, ten JPGs, a portrait, and a workshop proposal form listing materials costed for six people and the space the session needs. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: Free to apply (€500 if selected). Prize: 8-day residency + Exhibition.

item.title: Experimental Photo Festival 2027 — Artists Open Call
item.description: The eighth Experimental Photo Festival runs in Barcelona from July 21 to 25, 2027, and this is the call for the artists who build its programme — distinct from the festival's exhibition call. It is international and aimed at photographers, visual artists, multidisciplinary artists and collectives who explore, question or transform photography through technique, materials, concept, technology or interdisciplinary practice; the festival says you do not have to call yourself an experimental photographer to apply. A proposal is not a portfolio submission: each applicant proposes two workshops — one of four hours, built on a technique, process or methodology they know well, and one of eight hours that lets participants go deeper into a process, research or experimental approach — plus one discursive activity, either a conference, a roundtable or a project or research presentation, lasting 20 to 40 minutes. Each workshop carries a materials budget of up to €50 covered by the Experimentalphotofestival Association, and an exhibition proposal may optionally be included. Applying is free: the proposal form is a document downloaded from the festival's own call page and submitted through its online form together with a biography of up to 250 words in the applicant's own language, a PDF dossier, ten JPGs of the work and a portrait. SELECTED ARTISTS ARE PAID, AND CHOOSE BETWEEN TWO COMPENSATION OPTIONS: six nights in the festival's official accommodation (stated value €300) plus €200 in cash, or €500 in cash with accommodation arranged and paid by the artist. Either option also includes meals during the festival, full artist accreditation, official 2027 merchandise, and a place on the twelve-month Diploma in Experimental Photography at Ágora, School of Experimentation — more than 60 techniques and processes, specialisation, mentoring and a final personal project — which the festival values at €999. Travel to and from Barcelona is not covered, and payment requires an invoice issued in the artist's name. The festival publishes a financial transparency page stating that 94 people receive compensation through it — 50 artists, 14 staff and 30 volunteers — while 150 people pay a registration fee to attend. Selection is by the Experimentalphotofestival Association team against three criteria: connection to the festival's three challenges (combining knowledge and processes, building meaning beyond technique, and treating creation as a space for exchange), contribution to gender balance in the programme, and originality; applications are read individually and then weighed collectively against the whole 2027 programme. Selected artists must be in Barcelona from July 20 to 26, 2027, with July 20 given to workshop preparation, material review and technical checks, and sign an agreement covering activities, compensation, production, cancellation and image rights. Artists retain copyright and ownership of their work; the Association takes a non-exclusive right to reproduce submitted images, always credited, for promotion, exhibition and editorial use, and to record the festival itself. The call opened October 12 and selected artists are announced in December. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €200–€500.

item.title: Upside down · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition built on a single experimental hanging decision: the photographs are shown turned upside down. PH21's premise is that inverting an image strips it of its representative function — the depicted scene and objects become difficult, if not impossible, to recognise — while the formal and compositional aspects become more pronounced, directing attention away from scene and object recognition. Any photograph is eligible if the artist is willing to present it this way. Abstract photographs may be the most obvious candidates, but the call argues that depictive works can be appreciated in novel ways when inverted, and names landscapes, bodyscapes, symmetrical compositions, architectural and street photography as excellent candidates, with other genres also considered. The theme is broadly interpreted and independent of generic or stylistic constraints. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD in Philosophy, Rutgers; founder, director and curator of PH21 Gallery, a Photolucida Critical Mass juror since 2023 and invited to Photolucida's Board of Directors in 2026) and Borbála Jász (art historian and philosopher of art, PH21 vice-director, a Critical Mass juror since 2025 and also invited to the board in 2026). One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions are announced; the juror's choice receives three free entries to any upcoming PH21 themed group call, each covering up to 15 images. Entrants may submit 3, 5, 7, 10 or 15 images — individual works, or including a series of at most five photographs — by email after paying the fee. THE STANDARD FEE IS PRICED BY IMAGE COUNT AND RISES AFTER THE EARLY BIRD DEADLINE: until November 30 it is €25 for the first 3 images, €30 for 5, €35 for 7, €40 for 10 and €45 for 15; after November 30 every rung goes up €5, to €30 / €35 / €40 / €45 / €50, so the stored €25 floor is only available up to the early bird date and only for three images. A reduced rate of €15 (early bird) or €20 after it covers up to five images for students, unwaged persons and applicants from low-income economies — the gallery asks for no proof of eligibility and says it trusts the applicant's judgement. Early bird deadline November 30, final deadline December 7; all entrants are notified 10–15 days after the final deadline. The exhibition runs February 6 – March 2, 2027 at PH21's venue in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. Selected photographers pay a print and installation fee, from €45 for a matted print up to 40cm / 15.75in on the longest side, or may ship their own exhibit-ready prints; entering grants the gallery a non-exclusive promotional and exhibition licence with no royalties, copyright and ownership stay with the photographer, submitted work need not be for sale, and the gallery commission on any sale is 25%. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: True Blue · Cultural Center of Cape Cod
item.description: The Cultural Center of Cape Cod, a 501(c)(3) arts centre on a historic campus at 307 Old Main Street in South Yarmouth, Massachusetts, is running True Blue as an online juried exhibition: from the vastness of the sky to the depths of the sea, from loyalty and friendship to sorrow and melancholy, it asks artists to explore the colour, symbolism and emotional resonance of blue, and it wants interpretations ranging from the literal to the figurative. Photography is named in the eligible media alongside painting, drawing, digital art, mixed media, sculpture, fibre art, printmaking, glass, wood, ceramics and signed, numbered limited-edition prints; video is the only exclusion. Entry is $20 for the first work and $5 for each additional work up to a maximum of 20 images, non-refundable and no guarantee of acceptance. Awards are $300 for first place, $200 for second and $100 for third, and the first-place winner also has the option of showing the winning image — and possibly more, depending on size — for a month during 2027 in the Center's physical Showcase Gallery on the Cape Cod campus, which turns an online prize into a real wall. The virtual exhibition stays online for three months. Jurying is by the Cultural Center's directors, who give no individual feedback. Sales inquiries are routed to the artist, whose own link sits beside the image in the online gallery, and the Center takes no commission on an online sale; in exchange, entering grants the Cultural Center copyright in the image for display and promotional use, while the physical artwork stays the artist's property. Work that is copied, produced by AI, or made under an instructor's guidance is not eligible. Winners are notified and the online gallery opens by December 15, 2026. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $20 + $5 per additional work (up to 20). Prize: $300 / $200 / $100 + online exhibition + gallery month for 1st.

item.title: Small Wonders 2026 · Cultural Center of Cape Cod
item.description: Small Wonders is the Cultural Center of Cape Cod's juried small-works holiday exhibit, filling the Great Hall of its South Yarmouth campus from November 18 to December 19, 2026. There is no theme: the only rules are size and price. Work may be no larger than 12 inches on its longest side, though a frame may extend to 16 inches, and the Center suggests pricing at no more than $350 so that the show works as a place to buy art as a gift — buyers take pieces home immediately rather than waiting for the exhibit to close. Many media are welcome and photographs are named explicitly, alongside paintings, textiles, glass, sculpture, ceramics, collage, assemblage and mixed media; video is excluded. Entry is $10 per piece for up to five pieces, non-refundable even if the work is not accepted, and there is no online route: artists print the submission form from the Center's Call For Art page (or fill one in on arrival) and hand-deliver the work with payment on Monday, November 16, 10am to 4pm. Jurying and notification happen the next day, Tuesday, November 17, and work not taken into the show is collected on November 18, the day the exhibit opens; the reception is Friday, November 20, 5–7pm, and unsold work is picked up on December 21. All work must be for sale, with the Center taking 40% of the sale price and the artist 60%. Everything must be original, prints must be signed and numbered, wall work must be ready to hang (no saw-tooth hangers), and no AI-generated work is accepted. One clause lives only on the printed submission form rather than on the web page: work left beyond 90 days becomes the property of the Cultural Center unless alternate arrangements have been made, and the Center is not responsible for work left after the posted pickup date. The Center is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a year-round programme of exhibitions, classes, residencies and events on Cape Cod. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $10 per piece (up to 5). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 17th Big Gay Art Show · Sedona Arts Center
item.description: Sedona Arts Center's Big Gay Art Show was, in the centre's own words, originally envisioned in 2009 by a group of artists and community members — some affiliated with the centre, others with Sedona Pride — as an inclusive platform to uplift and amplify queer artists in the local arts scene; the centre's own CaFE listing for this edition instead dates that founding conversation to 2012, so treat the start year as the organisation's two surfaces leave it. It is now produced entirely by the arts centre at Sedona Pride's request, and the 17th edition hangs on-site at 15 Art Barn Road from June 4 to July 18, 2027, with an opening reception on June 4, 4–6pm. It is a juried exhibition and sale celebrating creative expression from the LGBTQIA+ community and its allies, and the centre is explicit that entry is not restricted to LGBTQ+ artists — the call is open to allies too, to artists of all backgrounds and experience levels, and to all mediums, with photography and digital media named among the media the centre's exhibitions carry. Entry is $40 for one submission of up to three JPEGs at a minimum 300 DPI, cropped to the artwork with no mat or frame, each file named with the piece's title and listed on the entry form with dimensions, medium and price. Artists must be 18 or older, the work must have been made in the last three years, and it cannot have hung in any previous Sedona Arts Center exhibition. Awards are First Place/Best of Show $500, Second $250 and Third $150, with honourable mentions at the jurors' discretion and a People's Choice announced at the end of the run. Notifications go out by May 7, 2027; accepted work must reach Sedona — shipped or hand-delivered — by June 2. All entries must be for sale at a price the artist sets, and the centre retains a 35% commission, paying out in the month following a sale — a lower cut than the 40% it takes on its Juried Friends Show. Shipping runs at the artist's expense in both directions: artists pay to get work to the centre and must supply a FedEx or UPS prepaid label for the return of unsold work. One eligibility caveat to settle before paying: the CaFE record for this call states only '18 years and older', while the centre's own Call to Artists page states eligibility for its juried exhibitions as 'U.S. artists, 18+' — the two surfaces disagree and the broader one is the call's own application document, so non-US photographers should confirm with the centre first. The centre asks selected artists to help promote the show through their own channels and states plainly that while it promotes the exhibition through press releases, mailings, its website and social media, it cannot guarantee any particular level of visibility. Sedona Arts Center has been a creative home in Sedona since 1958 — more than 68 years, by its own count — and is a nonprofit in Uptown Sedona whose gallery, in its own words, 'represents over 100 professional local and regional artists', with a ceramics studio operating continuously since 1958 and a 2026–27 exhibition schedule that also includes the Vision and Sound African American experience exhibit and the First Peoples Exhibit. — Deadline: May 1, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: $500 / $250 / $150 + exhibition.

item.title: 46th Annual Juried Friends Show · Sedona Arts Center
item.description: Sedona Arts Center's Juried Friends Show and Sale reaches its 46th year in 2027, hanging at the centre's gallery at 15 Art Barn Road in Uptown Sedona from March 5 to April 18, 2027, with an opening reception on March 5, 4–6pm. The theme this year is The Face of Friendship. It is open to artists of all levels working in all mediums — the centre's own exhibition listing names painting, sculpture, photography and digital media — but it is gated by support rather than by residency: every applicant must be a current Sedona Arts Center donor at the Friend level, which starts at $70, at the time of applying. On top of that the entry fee is $40 for one submission of up to three JPEGs at a minimum 300 DPI, cropped to the artwork without mat or frame, with title, dimensions, medium and price listed on the entry form. Artists must be 18 or older, the work must have been made within the last three years, and it cannot have been shown in any previous Sedona Arts Center exhibition. Awards are First Place/Best of Show $500, Second $250 and Third $150, with honourable mentions at the jurors' discretion and a People's Choice award announced at the end of the run. Notifications go out by February 12, 2027 and accepted work must reach Sedona, shipped or hand-delivered, by March 3. Everything in the show must be for sale at a price the artist sets, and the centre retains 40% commission, paying out in the month following a sale. Shipping runs at the artist's expense in both directions: artists pay to get work to Sedona and must supply a USPS, FedEx or UPS prepaid label for the return of unsold work. One eligibility caveat to settle before paying the $40 and the $70 donation: the CaFE record for this call states only '18 years and older', while the centre's own Call to Artists page states eligibility for its juried exhibitions as 'U.S. artists, 18+' — the two surfaces disagree and the broader one is the call's own application document, so non-US photographers should confirm with the centre first. Selected artists are asked to help promote the exhibition; the centre states plainly that it cannot guarantee any particular level of visibility despite its own press, mailing and social-media promotion. Sedona Arts Center has been a creative home in Sedona since 1958 — more than 68 years, by its own count — and its gallery, in its own words, 'represents over 100 professional local and regional artists'; its 2026–27 programme that also includes the Vision and Sound African American experience exhibit, the First Peoples Exhibit and the Big Gay Art Show. — Deadline: February 5, 2027. Fee: $40 (Friend-level donation required, from $70). Prize: $500 / $250 / $150 + exhibition.

item.title: PASSAGE 2027 · Sussex Contemporary
item.description: Sussex Contemporary's first exhibition of 2027 is also its first international open call: PASSAGE fills BN9 Studio in Newhaven, on the Sussex coast, from 6 to 28 March 2027, open to the public across four weekends. The theme is the single word — artists are invited to read it politically, personally or poetically, with the organisers stating there is no single right interpretation. What makes this unlike most open calls is that it is what Sussex Contemporary calls democratic: there is no jury and no pre-selection, so once you buy an entry your work is in the show. The only limit is space — a maximum of 300 submissions, and entries close when those 300 places are filled or at 23:59 on 31 January 2027, whichever comes first. Entry is priced by the space a work occupies rather than by medium: £20 for small work up to A4, £40 up to A2, £80 up to A0, measured including frame, plinth or mount, and if a piece falls between two sizes the larger tier applies. Each artist may enter a maximum of two works, and both 2D and 3D work is welcome — photography is named alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, sculpture, jewellery, illustration and mixed media. Entries are bought through the organisation's own online shop; a confirmation email is followed by a second email linking a private artists' page that carries the submission form, where the image and the work's details are uploaded (one form per entry purchased, and that information builds the catalogue). Every entry includes a copy of the printed exhibition catalogue, which features all works in the show, two invitations to the private view, and inclusion in the exhibition artwork list. All work is for sale and Sussex Contemporary takes 30% commission, with sold pieces staying on the wall until the show closes. Read the organisation's terms before entering, because the collection clauses carry money the call page does not mention: any work not removed by the final collection date is charged £15 per week or part week per piece; unsold work left more than 28 days past that date is deemed abandoned, and Sussex Contemporary may then sell or dispose of it and keep the proceeds; and where a sold piece is not collected by its buyer and the organisation has to ship it back to you, you pay transport and insurance plus a £25 administration fee. Artists deliver and collect their own work, gallery-ready and correctly prepared for display, on drop-off dates communicated to entrants. The exhibition is curated — hung and laid out — by Jo Myles, Sussex Contemporary's creative director, and follows two earlier democratic shows at the same venue, Meander and Efflorescence. This is the same organisation behind the judged Unfold open call with Fabrica in Brighton; PASSAGE is the unjuried, pay-to-exhibit end of its programme, and photographers should weigh the entry price against the fact that inclusion is guaranteed rather than selected. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: £20 / £40 / £80 (A4 / A2 / A0). Prize: Exhibition + catalogue.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — High-Speed Wildlife
item.description: Submit up to 5 images on the theme of high-speed wildlife — animals and birds caught in fast motion, from flight and leaping to hunting and running — for the 'One Thing This Month' reader competition (OP 335) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). The winner receives a SanDisk Extreme 1TB Portable SSD (RRP £233). The challenge is pegged to the main technique feature in that issue of the magazine, and entrants are asked to type the competition theme into the corresponding field on the submission form. Entries need captions of up to 75 words covering where, why and how each image was taken, plus full technical details in the magazine's stated order (camera and lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture, tripod or handheld). Free to enter, uploaded in bulk through the magazine's Google Form, which requires a Google account because uploads run through Google Drive. The magazine publishes work taken outside in the landscape, wildlife, nature, adventure and travel genres — not fashion, wedding, field sports or interiors — and asks that images be made ethically and with sensitivity to environmental and conservation issues. Image manipulation is allowed but the magazine favours a gentle, sophisticated approach to editing. Entry is restricted to readers aged 18 or over, with one entry per person per competition, and the publisher's competition terms state that winners are notified by email within 30 days of the closing date and have 14 days to claim the prize. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: SanDisk SSD (£233) + Publication.

item.title: AWD Members' Holiday Salon 2026 · Art Works Downtown
item.description: Art Works Downtown's salon-style member showcase fills the Founders' Gallery, Donors' Gallery and Artist's Wall of its San Rafael art center from November 27 through January 18, opening in time for holiday gift-buying and staying up through San Francisco Art Week. There is no application or review process — AWD's own directions tell members to "select the work that inspires you" — so any current member whose piece meets the size rules is in the show, which makes this an unusually low-friction way for a Bay Area photographer to get work on a gallery wall. Entry is free; what gates it is membership, $100 a year, open to working artists living within 100 miles of San Rafael. One original work per artist, and not a piece shown here in a previous year: 2D wall work must be 24 inches or smaller in any direction including frame and all materials, delivered dry, wired, framed and labelled on the back with the artist's name, hand-delivered to 1337 Fourth Street on November 14, 18, 19 or 20 and collected January 20–23 (unretrieved work is charged $5 a day in storage and becomes AWD property after 30 days). Two receptions run alongside the 2nd Friday Art Walk, on December 11 and January 8, and the exhibition is the centrepiece of Marin Art Day on Sunday, January 17, 2027, when 35+ open studios, artist talks and programming bring collectors and Bay Area audiences through the building. Work is for sale: AWD processes the transaction, reports the sales tax and passes the net to the artist, who is then responsible for donating 40% of that net back to the organisation; patrons may take a piece away before the show closes for gift-giving. Applying permits AWD to use images of accepted work in its promotion, and the organisation disclaims responsibility for loss or damage. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free (AWD membership required, $100/year). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Deck the Walls 2026 · Arts Foundation of Cape Cod
item.description: The Arts Foundation of Cape Cod’s annual holiday art auction returns, with bidding online and in person and a buy-now option, and the foundation makes a point of opening it to artists near and far rather than keeping it regional. Photography is named among the welcome media, alongside acrylic, oil, watermedia, pastel, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, fibre, wood, metal, glass, ceramics and jewellery; work must be original and ready to hang. Unusually for a holiday show, there is no maximum size — the foundation says outright that this is not a typical small-works holiday show and pieces of any size are welcome — and its experience is that work priced between $300 and $2,000 sells well here. Submission is free and an artist may put forward up to three pieces, though in most cases only one is chosen; space is limited and the foundation’s committee retains full discretion over selection. Each artwork is submitted with up to three JPEGs, a main shot plus up to two details, at least 2000 pixels on the longest side and under 5 MB, since the images are used for the online sale. Selected artists are notified by email on November 13; work is dropped off on November 16 at the Sketch Pad on Pearl Street in Hyannis or shipped to arrive by November 23 at the artist’s expense with a prepaid return label. The public preview goes online November 20, the buy-now event runs November 27 to December 11, and an open house is held at the Sketch Pad on Saturday, December 5. The money terms are not on the call page — they sit in the Submittable guidelines, and they matter: the foundation asks artists to donate 100% of the sale proceeds, and states that “the option for the artist to receive 25% or 50% of the sale value is also available”, chosen on the submission form, so the most an artist can keep is half. Bidding opens at 60% of the value the artist states, with an optional reserve price below which the work will not sell — the foundation’s own worked example is a $1,000 artwork opening at $600, where an $800 sale on the 50% option returns $400 to the artist. Sales are confirmed by December 16 with cheques mailed within 30 days; unsold work is returned or donated to the foundation according to the artist’s stated preference, and the rest of the proceeds support its work across the region’s arts and cultural community. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + up to 50% of sale price.

item.title: What Would You Do With $1000 · No More Starving Artists Foundation
item.description: A microgrant from the No More Starving Artists Foundation, a Palm Beach County 501(c)(3) whose stated mission is to help artists build a sustainable practice and a lasting legacy. The $1,000 award is deliberately open-ended: it is meant to fund the creation of new work, the completion of a project already under way, professional development, or a new experimental concept that pushes the artist’s work forward. It is open to professional artists over 18 who live in Palm Beach County only, at emerging, mid-career or established stage, and across every discipline the foundation lists — visual artists, musicians, vocalists, literary artists, designers, dancers, culinary artists, poets, writers and filmmakers — so photographers apply as visual artists. Applicants must not be currently enrolled in an active educational programme, and may only apply as a solo artist: no collaborations and no teams. All submitted works, concepts and accompanying materials must be original and, in the foundation’s words, conceived and executed solely by human hands, minds or voices — generative AI is explicitly barred. The application asks for an artist statement (not a bio or résumé), a detailed written description of the specific idea the artist wants to realise and why the funding matters for it, a short 30-to-60-second proposal video to accompany that narrative, and three work samples. The entry fee is $10 and non-refundable; the number of awards is not fixed and jurors are to be announced. Recipients also receive a one-year NMSAF membership. The award is not an unconditional grant: the foundation's legal agreement binds every recipient to a Pay It Forward commitment to volunteer in the community within 12 months and to file documented proof of it — a signed letter from the organisation served, or five photographs, or a video — and states that if the proof is not provided, “the entire grant will revert to a loan and must be repaid to NMSAF”, with a 1.5% monthly finance charge on any delinquent balance. Recipients also file a W-9. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $1,000 + one-year NMSAF membership.

item.title: Artist Accelerator Program Spring 2027 · Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description: SebArts’ Artist Accelerator is a free, three-month professional development cohort for Sonoma County artists, built to move a practice toward being sustainable as well as creative: artistic development, financial management, marketing and sales, social media, curatorial guidance in the art market, collector relationships, critiques and exhibition opportunities. New for this cycle, accepted artists also receive a $500 stipend. The Spring 2027 cohort runs April 1 to June 30, 2027, takes six to eight artists, and meets for a minimum of four hours a week — typically Tuesdays noon to 2pm and Thursdays 10am to noon, with additional events and some evening sessions — at the centre’s building on South High Street in Sebastopol, California. Applicants must be 18 or over, live in Sonoma County, and be available for the full term; artists at any career stage are encouraged, professional and non-professional alike, and all creative disciplines are welcome, so photographers are eligible. The application is free and asks for a short narrative on the artist’s background and focus, two to ten work samples, a résumé, and a signed letter of support or testimonial from someone familiar with the applicant’s work who can speak to its practice, relevance and community impact, including their name, title and contact details. The programme is sponsored by Creative Sonoma and the County of Sonoma; its workshop series is also offered free to the public by RSVP. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 stipend + professional development programme.

item.title: 2027 Mid-Atlantic Juried Show · McGuffey Art Center
item.description: The third annual Mid-Atlantic Juried Show at McGuffey Art Center, one of the oldest artist-run cooperative art centres in the United States, housed in a historic elementary school building in downtown Charlottesville, Virginia. The show runs April 2 to May 1, 2027, with a First Friday opening reception on April 2 from 5:30 to 7:30 pm and a panel discussion on the closing day. Any artist aged 18 or over resident in Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Washington DC or North Carolina may enter; photography is one of the seven named categories, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, fibre, sculpture and mixed media. Work must be original and made within the last three years, and AI-enhanced or AI-generated art and photography is prohibited from entry, as is work copied from other artists or from published material. Two-dimensional entries may not exceed eight feet in any direction and nothing requiring the artist to be present for moving or assembly is accepted. Entry is $35 for up to three submissions, reduced to $25 for McGuffey Art Center Association members via a coupon code from the front office, and only one piece per artist is taken into the exhibition. Accepted artists pay a $10 handling fee and arrange delivery themselves — hand-delivered March 25–27 or shipped prepaid March 22–26, in reusable containers with a return label — and the centre states it does not insure work in transit or on exhibit. Work is for sale unless marked otherwise, with the artist keeping 65% and McGuffey 35%. The 2027 juror is Jack Rasmussen, Director and Curator of the American University Museum at the Katzen Arts Center in Washington DC since it opened in 2005, previously Executive Director of Maryland Art Place and of di Rosa, and a past president of the Maryland State Arts Council; he judges on artistic voice and vision and on technical execution, and his decisions are final. Artists are notified on February 15, 2027. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $35 (up to 3 entries; $25 members) + $10 handling if accepted. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exploring Darkness and Shadows · L7 Gallery
item.description: L7 Gallery, a Bellingham, Washington space that shows neo-figurative, neo-expressionist, spiritual-abstraction and outsider work, invites international artists to its next online exhibition on the many meanings of darkness and shadow. The call sets the theme against the usual readings of fear, chaos and death: the night sky, fertile soil and the maternal womb are all dark places necessary for life. It leans on Jun’ichirō Tanizaki’s In Praise of Shadows — Eastern cultures preferring jade’s pensive luster to a shallow brilliance, tarnished silver over polish, aged grain over new wood — and on Romeo seeing Juliet hang upon the night like a jewel in an Ethiope’s ear, and it ranges its references from da Vinci, Vermeer and Goya to Vija Celmins, Astro Boy and Kara Walker. The gallery supplies definitions of skiagraphia, tenebrism, chiaroscuro and sfumato as starting points. Photography is named among the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, watercolour, sculpture, digital art, printmaking and fabric art. The juror is Jesse Firestone, Associate Curator of the RAY Triennial of Photographic Arts in Frankfurt and Curator of Exhibitions at The Interchurch Center in New York, who has organised more than 60 exhibitions and works on artist agency and experimental approaches to exhibition-making. First place takes a $300 award and two further artists receive honourable mentions. The call’s own timeline opens applications on 15 October 2026, closes them on 15 November, juries 16–19 November, notifies artists on 20 November and runs the online exhibition from 20 November to 31 December 2026. Entry is $30 for one to three images, all work must be original and artists must be 18 or over. Every piece must be for sale for the run of the show at a price fixed at application and cannot be withdrawn early; the artist keeps 60% of any sale, and submitting grants the gallery promotional use of the images. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $30 (1–3 images). Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals 2027–2028 · Winterville Cultural Center Gallery
item.description: The Winterville Cultural Center Gallery, in a renovated 1950s high school just outside Athens, Georgia, takes exhibition proposals year-round through an artist proposal form reached from the Call for Art panel on its gallery page. The form is headed “Artist Proposal Form (2027/28 consideration)” and opens by stating that all proposals currently submitted are being considered for 2027 and 2028, so there is no dated cutoff. Proposals may be for a solo show or for a group with named collaborators, and the form asks for contact details, a biography, a statement about the proposed exhibition, the exhibition title, the approximate size and number of pieces available, and how three-dimensional work would need to be displayed. Applicants upload ten examples: a group representative sends ten works that would be in the show, while an individual sends at least five images of the proposed work and five of earlier work. The form's own wording sets the file limit at 2 MB while the uploader beneath it enforces a maximum of 1 MB per file, so keep every file under 1 MB; PDF, image and video files are accepted. Submitting requires a Google account, because the form records the account name and email address when files are uploaded. There is no submission fee. The gallery's programme is two-dimensional and three-dimensional work across media and it names photography among the accepted media in its own national juried Small Works exhibition, so lens-based proposals are in scope. Selected artists are also asked whether they are willing to give an artist talk, run a demonstration or volunteer at the gallery desk. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Insho Works Prize
item.description: Insho is an independent online platform for short visual essays — three to twelve slides, read in under two minutes — and its curated Works section is running a free prize in two categories, Writing and Art. The Art category names photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics and other visual work, so a photo sequence or a small project built as a slide piece is exactly the format. There is no entry fee, and one piece may be entered in each category. Entrants build the work on the platform with a free account, each slide holding up to 600 characters and about 1,200 words across the piece, choose the Art category and submit to Works by 11:59 pm Eastern Time on 30 December 2026; submissions are reviewed before publishing and Works is curated, so not everything is accepted. Entry is open to anyone 18 or older, anywhere PayPal can send payments. The editor of Insho selects ten finalists in each category and the top three in each, judging on originality, craft and how well the piece uses the slide format; all finalists are featured on the platform, winners are announced in January 2027 and prizes are paid by PayPal within thirty days. Prizes are $300 for first place, $200 for second and $100 for third in each category. Work must be the entrant's own with rights to every element in it, and work published elsewhere before is welcome; AI-assisted editing tools are allowed but must be declared in the Credits field, and work generated entirely by AI is not eligible. Entrants keep ownership and grant Insho permission to feature the piece on the site and share it on the platform's social accounts with credit. The platform's guidelines also bar thin teasers, advertising and links to shops or ticketing pages, and ask that each piece stand on its own. — Deadline: December 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300 first prize + online publication feature.

item.title: Freezer Festival 2026 — VJ Books
item.description: Freezer Festival Internacional de Fotografía — now in its third edition, curated by photographer and teacher Luciana Demichelis — is looking for photographers and musicians to build a VJ book for its November 2026 programme. A VJ book, also called a bookjockey, is an experimental performance device: a video camera pointed at a table of objects, photographs, fanzines and photobooks, projected live, with a music set played alongside it. The festival has staged three of them so far — Federico Paladino with songs by Seba Rulli at Casa Unclan, curator Luciana Demichelis for the CEF Córdoba visit to the Centro de Arte UNLP, and photographer Amparo Fernández with photographs intervened live. This is the first year it is opened as a call. You can apply as a solo VJ (making the visuals and playing the music set yourself) or as a duo (one on live visuals, one on music). The festival supplies a webcam connected to a projector, a tripod and sound; the application form asks what else you need. Freezer runs from Thursday 5 to Sunday 15 November 2026 across La Plata, Berisso, Ensenada and Buenos Aires, with the Centro de Arte UNLP and the Edificio Karakachoff as its main venues, alongside photographic exhibitions, photobook presentations, open talks, workshops and photographic brigades. Proposals submitted here are also considered for the festival's presentations and curatorial projects through 2027. There is no entry fee. Selected artists are confirmed by email and on the festival's social channels. Applications close 31 October 2026 at 23:59. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Festival exhibition + performance slot.

item.title: Trailhead Gallery 2027 Call for Artists · The Loppet Foundation
item.description: The Loppet Foundation — a Minneapolis non-profit that runs year-round outdoor programming from Theodore Wirth Park under a public/private partnership with the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board — is booking its 2027 season at the Trailhead Gallery. The gallery sits inside The Trailhead, the Loppet's public building and the trail hub for walkers, skiers, bikers, runners and birdwatchers, so a show there is seen by thousands of park visitors across a four-to-six-week run. Photography is named among the accepted 2D media. The Art Committee gives priority to Minnesota artists whose work speaks to the connection between art and the outdoors, meaningful community connection outdoors, local flora and fauna, inclusion and diversity in the outdoors, sustainability and habitat restoration, wellness, or play. Eligibility as written is 'emerging and established artists in the Twin Cities and surrounding areas', and the Loppet states it strongly encourages BIPOC and Queer-identified artists to apply. Shows are 8–12 pieces, each no larger than 24 x 36 inches and up to 5 lbs, framed or otherwise ready to hang, with one or two larger works possible. Priority consideration goes to submissions emailed between 15 October and 15 November 2026; work sent after 15 November is still accepted and considered on a rolling basis as gallery space allows. This is an unpaid exhibition — there is no fee to apply and no stipend, and artists keep 100% of any sales made directly to buyers. Selection is by the Loppet's Art Committee, a volunteer group of artists, community members, and Minneapolis Park Board and Loppet staff. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Fotografia Calabria Festival Award 2026
item.description: Fifth edition of the award run by the Associazione Pensiero Paesaggio alongside Fotografia Calabria Festival, Calabria's first widespread photography festival (first edition 2022, grown out of the earlier Fiumefreddo Photo Festival). For the first time the competition sets no theme, asking instead for projects with strong conceptual coherence and a recognisable artistic vision; entries are judged on the quality and originality of the photographic research, narrative coherence and the strength of the proposal. Each photographer may enter one project of 10 to 25 images, shot digitally or on film (analogue work scanned), with diptychs allowed; post-production is accepted as an expressive choice, but in documentary projects removing or adding people or objects is not. The winner receives €2,000 in cash from the Festival plus a paid €1,000 commission to publish a project in Internazionale magazine — the two prizes may be combined or awarded separately — along with an exhibition or screening at a forthcoming edition of the Festival and twelve months of promotion. Shortlisted projects go into the permanent online gallery on the Festival's website and its social channels. Copyright stays with the photographer. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: €2,000 + publication in Internazionale + exhibition.

item.title: 53rd Annual Membership Exhibition · Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art
item.description: The Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art's 53rd annual exhibition of work by its own members, on view in the museum's galleries in Saint Joseph, Missouri from 16 January to 21 February 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 15 January from 4 to 7pm and an awards ceremony at 6pm that evening. Photography is category 5 of the ten entry categories, alongside oil and acrylic painting, watercolour, drawing, printmaking, pottery and ceramics, 2-D mixed media, digital art, fibre and textiles, and sculpture and 3-D mixed media; museum staff may reassign a work to the category they think fits. The exhibition is judged, and the entry form carries an opt-out box for artists who do not want their work considered for awards. Entry itself is free, but the show is open only to current AKMA members — new members may join at any time before the drop-off period, with individual membership at $35 a year, $15 for students with a student ID, $20 for teachers and $25 for anyone living more than 60 miles from Saint Joseph. Each individual membership may submit two artworks; a family or dual membership may submit two per person but no more than three as a household. Work must have been made in the last five years, must not have been shown at the museum before, and is capped at 4 by 4 feet including the frame and 50 pounds, with works on paper matted and framed behind glass or Plexiglass and 2-D work wired ready to hang. There is no entry portal: the completed, signed paper entry form is handed in with the artwork at the museum's front desk during the drop-off window of 6 to 10 January 2027, and work is collected again on 22, 23 or 24 February. Artists may mark a work for sale or not; the museum retains 30% on anything sold during the exhibition. Nothing may be removed before the exhibition closes, the museum does not store work, and anything not collected within 30 days is subject to disposal. The Albrecht-Kemper opened as the Albrecht Gallery in 1966 in the former Albrecht family home, took its present name in 1991, and holds one of the Midwest's finest collections of 18th- through 21st-century American art. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: Free (AKMA membership required, $35/year individual; $15 student). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 41st Annual All-Florida Exhibition · Alliance for the Arts
item.description: The Alliance for the Arts' flagship annual juried show, open to artists living anywhere in Florida and described by the organisation as "the most anticipated of the year" — work from across the 65,000 square miles of the state brought together as a portrait of contemporary Florida art. Photography is one of the named entry categories, alongside painting (oil, acrylic, collage, watercolour, mixed media), drawing, sculpture, ceramics, metalsmithing, glass, digital media, video, printmaking, fibre and textiles. An entry is one to three artworks: $25 for the first, $7 for each additional — though the CaFÉ checkout panel prices the extra works at $5, not $7, so budget for the organiser's higher figure and expect to be charged the platform's. Awards are $1,000 cash for Best in Show, a $300 Blick Art Materials gift certificate for second, $150 cash for third, and a Staff Choice award of a $75 artist membership. Only original work completed in the last two years and not previously shown at the Alliance is eligible; no giclée reproductions. Accepted 2D work must be wired and ready to hang and may not exceed six feet in any direction; 3D work is capped at six feet and 150 lbs. Artists pay their own shipping both ways. Every selected work must be offered for sale to the public at a price the artist sets — entries submitted not for sale are rejected — and the Alliance retains a 40% commission on works sold by non-members, 30% for members. The juror is not yet named. Notification by email on 9 February 2027, accepted work delivered 1 March, and the exhibition runs 5–27 March 2027 in the Alliance's Fort Myers galleries with an opening reception on 5 March. The Alliance for the Arts is a long-running non-profit arts centre on McGregor Boulevard with galleries, a theatre, an art house cinema, an outdoor ArtsPark and a weekly market; it also runs a standing, year-round call for curated-exhibition proposals in all media, photography explicitly among the themes it wants to explore. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $25 (1 entry) + $7 each additional. Prize: $1,000 Best in Show + $150 third place.

item.title: No-Type Artist Features — Open Call
item.description: Standing, free open call from No-Type, the independent Chicago photography publisher, for its Artist Features programme. The editors are "looking for new and exciting bodies of work from emerging and established photographers alike", and there are two outcomes: a FEATURE, which is a post carrying the work and the artist statement on No-Type's website and social media, or an INTERVIEW, which is everything in a feature plus a conversation about the artist's practice with editor Dylan Yarbrough. READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING: this call is not the printed magazine. The guidelines are titled "Artist Features" and the licence an applicant grants covers reproduction "on our social media and website as well as for related promotion and archival purposes" — No-Type's themed print issues run as separate, paid calls. There is no cash prize and no exhibition; what is on offer is a curated editorial feature from a publisher whose issues are real printed objects, at no cost to the photographer. Submissions are open on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline, reviewed monthly, and selected artists are contacted directly; the volume of submissions means no individual feedback on work that is not selected. Open to lens-based artists aged 18 and over from any country, emerging or established. Work must be made through a photographic or lens-based process — film, digital capture, archival materials, collage and alternative photographic methods are all named — while AI-generated images or work produced primarily through generative technologies are not eligible. Submit 15 to 20 images as a public link to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or similar, plus a single PDF combining an 80-120 word third-person bio and a 150-250 word statement; JPG, under 10 MB each, 2000 px on the longest side. Multiple submissions are permitted. Artists retain full copyright and are fully credited, and No-Type undertakes not to sell, license or distribute the images for any unrelated purpose without permission. The editors also state they will not edit or alter submitted images, though an image may appear as a cropped detail in a thumbnail or page design. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication feature.

item.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 76: Labour, Repetition and Print
item.description: UK-based independent art zine, edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers, calling for visual art and writing on labour, repetition and print. Print is framed here both as a medium and as a concept — "a mark left through pressure, contact, repetition or reproduction" — so a print can be an impression, a trace, a copy, a record, a pattern, a surface or evidence of an action. The editors want work on repetitive labour and routine; manual, industrial and domestic work; invisible, unpaid and care work; the process of making and skilled labour; printmaking, stamping, copying and seriality; digital reproduction and the circulation of images; and repetition as ritual, habit or compulsion. They ask what it means to make something by hand in an automated, digitally reproduced world, and how repetition might become a strategy for resistance, survival, memory or transformation. ALL MEDIA WELCOME, with photography named explicitly in the list alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, installation, text, film, video, animation, digital art, sound, performance, textile, ceramics, collage and written work; they particularly welcome work that challenges conventional definitions of what constitutes a print, an artwork, or an act of labour. Open internationally to emerging, mid-career and established artists, and explicitly to students, recent graduates and self-taught artists. Free to enter and free if selected. Submit one to three artworks with a statement of up to 300 words explaining how the work connects to the theme; writers may send prose up to 1,000 words or up to three poems. An Instagram handle is a stated requirement — the editors will not select artists without one, because selected work is tagged across their 11,000-follower platform. There is no cash prize: selected works appear in a curated online group exhibition on haus-a-rest.com and across the zine's social channels, typically online for about six months, and artists retain all rights. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: The Landscape: Serene and Savage · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on landscape in both its tranquil and its ferocious registers — gardens, seacoasts and sunsets as readily as thunderstorms, cliffs and floods, with human figures absent, dominant or diminutive. Seascapes, architectural elements, single flowers, trees, birds, animals, reflections and shadows all qualify, in any style from representational to abstract. Photography is one of the accepted media alongside painting, printmaking, sculpture and mixed media, and the gallery sets no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents 18 and over; $35 for three images, $5 for each additional up to nine. An Art of Distinction award gives one artist a special exhibit in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two, a $200 Director's Choice may be granted at the executive director's discretion, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity goes to one artist drawn from everyone exhibited at MVA during the calendar year, and honourable mentions are granted free entry to a future MVA show. Accepted artists ship at their own expense and must enclose a prepaid UPS or FedEx return label, and sales are split 70/30 in the artist's favour. Notification on or about January 26, 2027; exhibition April 4–28, 2027. The jurors have requested anonymity. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition opportunity.

item.title: The Human Family: International Photography Exhibition 2027 · Saturday Review Magazine
item.description: Saturday Review — the magazine founded in 1924 and now being relaunched as a quarterly print journal, with Issue No. 1 due Spring 2027 — is building an international photographic project around one question: what makes us human? Photographers worldwide are invited to submit images about connection, family, work, joy, struggle, ritual, solitude, community, ageing, childhood, culture and identity, documentary or artistic, intimate or expansive. Up to three photographs per €5 entry. Jurying is by Ned Rifkin, the magazine's art editor and former director of the Hirshhorn Museum and Under Secretary for Art at the Smithsonian. One grand prize of €1,000 is awarded and the winning work published in Saturday Review; further selected photographs are published in the magazine and its online gallery. Photographers keep full copyright and grant a non-exclusive licence for the magazine, exhibitions and promotion; book or print-sale use needs a separate agreement. Entries opened 10 October 2026 and close 15 March 2027; results 15 April 2027. — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: €5. Prize: €1,000 + publication.

item.title: Beca Joana Biarnés 2026 · Fundación Photographic Social Vision
item.description: The eighth edition of the grant the Fundación Photographic Social Vision created in 2019 in honour of Joana Biarnés, Spain's first woman photojournalist, who asked before her death that the proceeds of her work be used to strengthen the future of photojournalism. It funds an in-depth photojournalistic investigation carried out inside Spanish territory on a subject of current social relevance. The winner — an individual or a team — receives €8,000 to carry out the work over a maximum of nine months, mentoring throughout from a tutor with extensive teaching and professional experience, the temporary loan of photographic equipment from Foto Ruano Pro, and a guarantee that the finished project will be published in whatever format suits it best. Up to three finalists, the winner included, each get a portfolio review with an expert of their choosing from the foundation's list of collaborators, free access to the narrative-journalism workshop run by the independent magazine 5W and three months of its online subscription. Applicants must be between 18 and 35 years old inclusive and tax-resident in Spain; applications are direct from the author or authors, one proposal each, and in collective projects every member must meet the conditions and one acts as spokesperson. The jury looks for an unpublished subject or a genuinely new perspective on a familiar one, a project still in its early stages with most of the photographic research ahead of it, and work that has not yet received any national or international prize; the outcome must include an extensive series of still photographs, with multimedia accepted only as a complement. Methodology counts: the proposal has to identify expert sources by name, and the funded investigation must include at least two interviews with relevant specialists. The application is entirely free and can be made in Spanish or in Catalan with a Castilian version attached, as a set of PDFs — a CV carrying the ID number, address and date of birth of each participant; a portfolio of at least 25 images of previous work, noting what has already been published; a project presentation with title, justification, motivation in no more than 200 words, methodology and sources, visual approach, and a nine-month schedule and budget; plus a portrait and three photographs of your own connected to the theme, for promotion if you are shortlisted. Everything is sent by WeTransfer or a Dropbox or Drive link, emailed from the applicant's own address. The call runs from 14 September to 16 November 2026. The eighth-edition jury is Bego Antón, Olmo Calvo, Gorka Lejarcegi, María Santoyo and Jordi Rovira. The winner grants the foundation non-exclusive reproduction rights for its own communications and must credit the grant in any publication of the work. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €8,000 + 9-month mentoring + equipment loan.

item.title: HK Photozine & Photobook Dummy Award 2027 · Hong Kong Photobook Festival
item.description: The Hong Kong Photobook Festival's flagship award, open worldwide and free to enter this edition — "The application fee is waived this year" — with only shipping at the applicant's own cost. There are three routes in one call: the Photobook Dummy Award, and the Photozine Award in an Open and a Student category, the latter restricted to full-time students who upload proof of enrolment. The Dummy Award jury shortlists at most 15 finalists, the Photozine Award 10 per category, and three winners are then chosen from each; all finalists' work is exhibited at the Hong Kong Photobook Festival 2027, and the organisers note that previous years' winning and shortlisted dummies have toured to New Zealand, Germany, India, Indonesia, Taiwan, Brazil, Switzerland, Norway and Thailand. Winners get professional exchange with the jury and present their process to the festival audience. The first prize of the Photobook Dummy Award is a subsidy of up to HK$20,000 towards visiting an international photobook festival or self-publishing the book; the Photozine first prize is up to HK$3,000 per category. There is no age or nationality limit. A dummy may be made individually or collectively, must be original, must be self-published or unpublished with no publishing commitment to any registered publisher, may be in any language, needs no ISBN, and must have been created on or after 1 January 2024. A photozine must not exceed 32 pages, must have been created on or after 1 January 2026, and this year's Photozine theme is "Hong Kong". You may apply for both awards but each work may enter only one, and only one entry per award per applicant. Entry is two steps: an online registration form in Chinese or English with a PDF of all pages plus a cover image, then a physical copy with the registration proof in a sealed envelope marked with the award name, which must arrive at the organiser's Wan Chai address by post or in person by 31 January 2027 at 18:00 Hong Kong time — late or incomplete entries are declined. Shortlisted applicants then send a second physical copy within 21 days of the shortlist announcement so the work can tour. Applications opened 1 October 2026; finalists are announced in April 2027 and winners in May 2027. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free (shipping at your cost). Prize: HK$20,000 subsidy + festival exhibition.

item.title: FUTURES Nordic Talents 2027 · Copenhagen Photo Festival
item.description: Copenhagen Photo Festival nominates four Nordic photographers and lens-based artists each year to the FUTURES platform, the European network of photography organisations, and this is the open call for the 2027 cohort. Membership carries an artist fee of €500 and access to online conversations with experts, tutoring sessions, the annual FUTURES platform event, events hosted by the network's other member organisations and FUTURES meet-ups, plus continuous promotion on the platform's website, social media and print material; members can also enter two open calls exclusive to FUTURES artists, one for a travelling exhibition that moves between partnering venues across the year and one for an annual exhibition. On top of that the festival gives the nominated artists a screening of their submitted work during Copenhagen Photo Festival 2027, publication in the FUTURES archive on the CPF site, promotion on CPF's channels, free entry to the 2027 festival, an invitation to the festival's networking days and a portfolio session with Maja Dyrehauge Gregersen. Three eligibility conditions all have to hold: you have been resident in Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway or Sweden for at least the past 12 months; you were born in 1988 or later; and you have either studied photography or art, or your CV shows continual professional experience over the last three years, such as taking part in an exhibition or a publication. Applicants who entered previous FUTURES open calls may apply again unless they were previously selected as platform members. The application is a single PDF of at most 10 MB — CV and bio on no more than two pages, a project description on no more than one page, and 10 to 20 photographs from your latest or current project — submitted through the festival's own form with a DKK 100 administrative fee. The organisers ask for a cohesive photography or art project with a conceptual background that relates to your wider practice, ongoing or new. The festival's Programme Committee, whose members work in curation, publishing and visual storytelling, makes the selection; applicants hear back in mid-December 2026 and the four talents are announced in February 2027, ahead of the November 2027 festival. Previous CPF nominees include Emma Sarpaniemi, Inuuteq Storch, Jenni Toivonen and María Kristín Antonsdóttir. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: DKK 100. Prize: €500 + FUTURES platform membership + CPF 2027 screening.

item.title: ART WEIRD AND WILD · MVA Gallery
item.description: A national call from the MVA Gallery in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania for the strange and the unconventional: "If your art is strange or unconventional, this is the exhibition for you. Please share your weird and wild images with the Gallery's art enthusiasts and collectors." The gallery places the show in the lineage of Surrealism, Dadaism, Expressionism, Metaphysical Painting and Magic Realism, and offers a long but open list of directions — dreams, nightmares and the unconscious; enigmatic landscapes; mysterious and supernatural scenes; bizarre creatures; eerie light and shadow; distortion and fragmentation; unexpected colour combinations; visual narratives of alienation, anger and psychological distress; subverted perspective; personal references to memory, eroticism and childhood; surprising juxtaposition of objects; metamorphosis of people, animals and objects — "and anything else -- ordinary or eccentric, subtle or dramatic -- that excites you. You have limitless creative freedom for this exhibition." Photography is a named medium and the prospectus is unusually welcoming about process and presentation: "All photographic processes are welcome", with framing in black or white preferred for a traditional presentation, white or off-white mats, and unframed mounting considered. There is no cutoff date for when the work was made, and work previously shown at MVA is not eligible. A small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers, curators and academics juries the entries and has requested anonymity for this show; decisions are final and no feedback is given. Awards are an "Art of Distinction" award — a featured solo presentation in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date — a $200 Director's Choice award at the Executive Director's discretion, honourable mentions that carry free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity chosen in December from everyone exhibited that calendar year. The exhibition runs 4–28 April 2027; artists are notified on or about 23 February 2027 and accepted work must reach the gallery by 31 March. Work has to arrive ready to hang with stretched wire on the back, under 48 inches framed and 45 lbs, plexiglass preferred over glass; sculpture is capped at 28 inches in any dimension. Artists pay shipping and insurance both ways and must enclose a prepaid return label. The gallery keeps 30% on sales. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Nikon Fotobus Grant 2026
item.description: A project-continuation grant for emerging photographers from Fotobus e.V., the Hannover-based photography society, funded with Nikon. Three awards are made — €5,000, €3,000 and €2,000 — and each of the three funded projects also receives a Nikon camera, with the full sum paid out immediately on announcement and no restrictions on how it is spent. What is funded is the continuation of a photographic project already under way: all genres of photography are welcome, group applications from two or more photographers are allowed, and the work may use text, found images, documents or drawings alongside the photographs as long as its core is photographic. Video works are not accepted and AI-generated images are excluded outright — the society funds photography only — while manipulation and staging are permitted in conceptual work provided they are disclosed in the captions; applicants also accept the World Press Photo Code of Ethics. Eligibility runs on either of two alternatives, with nationality irrelevant to both: being enrolled as a student at a university in Germany, Austria or Switzerland at the time of applying (no age limit, and any subject, not only photography), or being no older than 30 and resident in Germany, Austria or Switzerland. Membership of Fotobus is not required. One application per person, though you may additionally join a group application, and an unfunded project may be entered again next year. The application is free and goes only through Picter: a project description of up to 3,000 characters answering the organisers' set questions, a maximum of 30 images from the unfinished project, and a CV of up to 1,500 characters — the quality of the edit and the sequence are explicitly part of the jury's assessment. The jury meets in mid-November, a shortlist of 20 is published on 1 December 2026 and the three funded projects on 15 December 2026, with the one-year funding period running to 15 December 2027 and a final report due at the end of it. NOTE ON THE CLOSING DATE: the organiser's own page advertises 1 November 2026 at 23:59 German time, but the Picter form that applications must go through is set to close on 31 October at 23:59 German time — treat 31 October as the operative date. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 / €3,000 / €2,000 + Nikon camera.

item.title: VI Premio Editorial de Fotografía Documental Galega · FFoco Festival
item.description: The sixth edition of the Galician Documentary Photography Publishing Prize, run by the non-profit Asociación Recreativo Cultural Acolá — the association behind FFoco, the A Coruña photography festival, which marks its tenth edition at the Fundación Luis Seoane between October and December 2026 — and financed in full by the Fundación Marta Ortega Pérez. The prize exists to turn a documentary project into a book: entrants are not expected to arrive with a finished, print-ready dummy, and the organisers describe the call as accompanying a project until it acquires new value in book form. Open to photographers and collectives whose work is connected to Galicia, satisfying at least one of three conditions — born in Galicia, resident in Galicia, or presenting a project centred on or thematically and conceptually linked to Galicia. Subject matter is free, but the work must be documentary, original and previously unpublished in book form with no edition committed to a third party; earlier showing in exhibitions, magazines, digital publications or social media does not disqualify a project as long as the author still holds the rights needed to publish it as a book. Entry is a single PDF of at most 20 MB containing an essay or maquette of 30 to 60 photographs, plus a project description and a biography of up to 300 words each. An independent jury of publishing professionals and representatives of established imprints picks up to eight finalists and then one winner, judging technical quality, originality, narrative capacity, coherence and editorial viability; the jury's composition is published with the result and its decision is final. The winning project is published by the Galician imprint Alauda Negra with Acolá covering every editorial and production cost — image editing and selection, editorial direction and design, layout, pre-press, paper, printing and distribution — and the winner also receives €1,000 for the publishing rights under an editorial contract. Non-winning projects keep all their rights. The five previous winners are Ana Paes, Ana Núñez Rodríguez, the Cadela Negra collective, Iván Nespereira and Jesús García. Submissions close Sunday 18 October 2026 at 23:59 peninsular Spanish time. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Photobook published by Alauda Negra + €1,000.

item.title: Open Call Pop-up-Galerien Herbst 2027 — Waldviertel/Industrieviertel · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for the two pop-up galleries Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich runs in Bad Fischau-Brunn (Industrieviertel) and Horn (Waldviertel). In the second half of 2027 each gallery gives three artists a four-week exhibition — six slots in all — with the exact periods still to be announced ("Im zweiten Halbjahr 2027 bieten beide Galerien jeweils drei Künstlerinnen bzw. Künstlern die Möglichkeit zu einer vierwöchigen Ausstellung"). The 2027 edition keeps the existing free exhibition offer for members — "Das kostenlose Ausstellungsangebot für Mitglieder bleibt bestehen" — and adds a sharper focus on the artists themselves: "Neu ist der stärkere Fokus auf die Künstlerinnen und Künstler, ihre Arbeitsweisen und die mediale Begleitung der Ausstellungen." WHAT THEY WANT: "Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Persönlichkeiten hinter den Arbeiten" — the people behind the work, their artistic positions and personal approaches made visible. The gallery room can be drawn deliberately into the exhibition concept, and an idea for a mediation format the artist can run independently is a required part of the submission. NO MEDIUM IS NAMED AND NONE IS EXCLUDED: the call addresses "Künstlerinnen und Künstler sowie Kunsthandwerkerinnen und Kunsthandwerker" — artists as well as craftspeople — so a photographic project competes on the same terms as any other, and the Horn gallery's own 2026 programme included Fotoclub VHS Horn; what is being judged is an exhibition concept for a specific room, not a set of images. WHO CAN APPLY: artists from the Industrieviertel for the Bad Fischau-Brunn gallery and from the Waldviertel for Horn — each region is tied to one venue — and membership of Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich is a condition of entry ("Mitgliedschaft bei der Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich erforderlich"), €25 a year for artists and individuals on the organisation's own membership form. WHAT A SELECTED ARTIST GETS: the exhibition space free of charge, support with press and public relations, and professional atelier and portrait photographs plus a short video about their way of working, played in the gallery through the exhibition and given to the artist afterwards. WHAT IS ASKED IN RETURN is more than hanging work: the artist installs and dismantles the show themselves ("Selbstständiger Auf- und Abbau der Ausstellung") and organises both the vernissage and the finissage, with compulsory attendance on those two weekends at set hours — Saturday and Sunday 17:00–19:00 in Bad Fischau-Brunn, Saturday 17:00–19:00 and Sunday 15:00–17:00 in Horn — plus coordination with Kulturvernetzung, taking part in the video and photos, and promotion through the artist's own network. A further event, such as an artist talk, workshop or guided tour, is "erwünscht, aber keine Voraussetzung". SUBMIT: one PDF of no more than 8 MB with contact details, an exhibition concept with images running to at most two A4 pages, portfolio and CV, and the mediation-format idea, by email to the separate address published for each region.
