Selection is notified in early 2027; neither the listing nor the call's own PDF names a jury. — Deadline: November 19, 2026. Fee: Free (Kulturvernetzung NÖ membership required, €25/year individual). Prize: Four-week exhibition + atelier video and professional photos.

item.title: Kala Yatra International Artist Residency 2026/27
item.description: Year-round residency in the Kathmandu valley with Kala Yatra (कला यात्रा, “Art Journey”), an artist-run not-for-profit collective that curates concept-based exhibitions, socially relevant projects and residencies alongside workshops and educational outreach. The collective says residents “will benefit from a supportive art community and valuable resources” and that it prioritises “not only your artistic endeavors but also the relationships and collaborations that may emerge”, with the chance to explore Nepal's contemporary art scene, cultural diversity and geography. The residency offers networking opportunities and presentations at Kala Yatra and partner institutions, and says it can facilitate exhibitions or help residents navigate galleries and studios. Accommodation is an individual bedroom with linens, private or shared bathroom depending on the booking, a shared kitchen, a common working space, solar hot water, wi-fi (bring your own laptop), weekly housekeeping and a digital guidebook; airport pick-up and drop-off are available at extra cost. THE ARTIST PAYS: “We run an artist-led, self-funded residency and currently have no available funding. To cover administrative and utility expenses, we charge a minimal fee based on the duration of your stay” - €200 for two weeks, €400 for a month, and a reduced €300 a month for artists who are both residents and citizens of the SAARC countries (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka). There is no application fee and applications are accepted all year, by email: artist statement, CV or bio with a portfolio or website link, up to ten recent works in a single PDF, a copy of a valid passport and the collective's application form. Stays start at a minimum of two weeks and the collective asks artists to apply at least three months ahead because slots fill; the residency fee covers none of the airfare, visa fees, health insurance, local transport, food, materials or project costs, and airport pick-up is €25 on pre-booking. The programme is “open to, but not limited to” visual artists, painters, sculptors, ceramists, printmakers, performing artists, musicians, writers, new media artists, curators, filmmakers, theatre artists, architects, art critics and researchers, and invites anyone whose practice is not on that list to write in; a current resident is credited on the residency's own page as a “Visual Artist, Writer & Photographer”. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: €200 (2 weeks) / €400 per month (€300 per month for SAARC artists). Prize: Residency.

item.title: SÍM Residency — January–March 2027
item.description: Open call for one- to three-month residency stays in January, February and March 2027 at the SÍM Residency in Reykjavík, run by SÍM – the Association of Icelandic Visual Artists. The programme describes itself as “one of the Nordic region's most established artist residency programmes, welcoming around 200 artists and cultural practitioners from around the world each year”, and it offers private and shared studios, accommodation, an orientation meeting, an artist page on the residency's own website and social channels, and opportunities for public presentations and artist talks. It is open to “all creators and art practitioners” working in “all mediums of visual arts, design, architecture, music, dance, performance art, creative writing, curation, cultural work, and scientific research”; photographers are among the residents the programme publishes, including projects built by “repeatedly assembling, photographing, dismantling, and reassembling” found Icelandic materials and a multidisciplinary body of work made “through painting, photography, and printmaking”. THE ARTIST PAYS: SÍM is a nonprofit, self-funded programme with only partial facility support from the City of Reykjavík, so applying is free but a selected artist owes a 50,000 ISK non-refundable programme fee within 15 days of acceptance plus a monthly accommodation fee of 140,000 ISK for a single bedroom-studio and 210,000-280,000 ISK for a twin - the first month payable two months before arrival, also non-refundable. BUDGET THE HIGHER FIGURE: the page prints its room prices twice and the two tables disagree on two of the twins - the application form's own room selector charges 240,000 ISK for bedroom 18 and for bedroom-studio 2, where the Residency Fees block lists them at 210,000 and 230,000 - so one month in the cheapest room costs at least 190,000 ISK all in. The fee covers administration, a SÍM membership card, wi-fi, parking, bedding and towels, communal kitchen equipment, laundry, heating, water and electricity and basic tools in the project space; meals, materials, insurance, travel, living costs and workshop fees are not included, and the fee “does not constitute rent” so a resident does not become a tenant. Applicants must hold at least a BA, though “exceptions may be made for self-taught artists who demonstrate high professionalism in their artistic practices, supported by a compelling CV and project proposal”. The application asks for a 400-word project description covering the conceptual framework, research questions and working methods, three images of previous work (10MB total) and a CV; proposals touching sustainability, ecology, global warming, geology, the environment, Icelandic culture or Nordic language are flagged as an advantage. January and February applications are reviewed as they arrive with a reply within two weeks, and the residency notes a vibrant shared-living environment with communal kitchens that may not suit everyone. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free to apply; ISK 50,000 programme fee + ISK 140,000–280,000/month accommodation if accepted. Prize: Residency.

item.title: ICP Curatorial Vision Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: A $10,000 scholarship from the International Center of Photography for one emerging curator, covering most of the $12,500 tuition for ICP's Online One-Year Certificate in Curatorial Practice in Photography. The award “supports an emerging curator in developing the critical perspectives, research, and curatorial approaches needed to engage with photography and visual culture today”, and ICP frames it as “contributing to a more diverse and expansive conversation around the photographic image”. One recipient is chosen on the strength of the application materials and portfolio, and finalists may be invited to a Zoom interview. Both the programme application (through SlideRoom, $60 fee) and the separate scholarship application must be submitted by 18 October 2026, so a recipient's remaining cost is $2,500 of tuition plus that application fee. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in ICP's One-Year Certificate programmes - part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible - and awards cannot be combined, so an applicant may receive only one. ICP encourages applicants to apply for every scholarship they are eligible for. Decisions arrive by email with the admission letter; ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: $10,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: ICP Image Text Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: A $10,000 scholarship from the International Center of Photography for one emerging writer, artist or image-maker working at the intersection of photography and language, covering most of the $12,500 tuition for ICP's Online One-Year Certificate in Writing and the Photographic Image. ICP describes it as supporting “emerging writers, artists, and image-makers in developing their critical voice at the intersection of photography and language”, with the aim of fostering “new perspectives on photography and its role in shaping how we understand and engage with the world”. One recipient is chosen on the strength of the application materials and portfolio, and finalists may be invited to a Zoom interview. Both the programme application (through SlideRoom, $60 fee) and the separate scholarship application must be submitted by 18 October 2026, leaving a recipient $2,500 of tuition plus that fee. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in ICP's One-Year Certificate programmes - part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible - and awards cannot be combined, so an applicant may receive only one. ICP encourages applicants to apply for every scholarship they are eligible for. Decisions arrive by email with the admission letter; ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: $10,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: ICP Latin Vistas Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: Up to ten $5,000 scholarships from the International Center of Photography for emerging curators, writers, photographers and image-makers from Latin America, applied against the $12,500 tuition of any of ICP's three Online One-Year Certificate programmes - Curatorial Practice in Photography, Writing and the Photographic Image, or Documentary Practice: Visual Storytelling. ICP describes the award as supporting applicants “committed to exploring new perspectives through photography and visual storytelling”, giving recipients “the opportunity to develop their practice, expand their critical and creative approaches, and engage with ICP's international community of image-makers”. It is open to applicants who are from and currently reside in Latin America. Recipients are chosen on the strength of the application materials and portfolio, and finalists may be invited to a Zoom interview. Both the programme application (through SlideRoom, $60 fee) and the separate scholarship application must be submitted by 18 October 2026; the $5,000 covers part of the tuition, so a recipient still pays the $7,500 balance plus the application fee. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in the One-Year Certificate programmes - part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible - and awards cannot be combined, so an applicant may receive only one, though ICP encourages applying for every scholarship for which you are eligible. Decisions arrive by email with the admission letter; ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: Up to 10 × $5,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: TOTALLY OPEN · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest, the artist-run 501(c)(3) creative research gallery in Cincinnati, reverses its own method for a third year running: instead of naming a theme and calling for work about it, it opens the call to anything and discovers the theme (or themes) afterwards, through the curatorial process. "Utilizing a reduced entry fee to lower certain barriers to access, this call is TOTALLY OPEN - completely open to any work, any media, and idea, under the umbrella of 'visual art'." Open to everyone internationally - "There is no limitation to this special call" - although artists living in Ohio, Kentucky and Indiana are pointed to the Regional Showcase that shares this exhibition slot. Selection is two-part: an anonymous several-member panel of professional and academic advisors with a broad range of expertise scores the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibit curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium with no strings attached, and one work in each of the season's nine exhibition periods takes a $1,000 Grand Jury Award, decided by a second-round jury of the top-scoring works - a process that "applies to all exhibitions during our 23rd season, beginning September 25, 2026, and continuing through August 2027, including this one". The exhibition runs 5 March - 2 April 2027; notifications are emailed to all entrants by 25 January 2027 and accepted work is due at the gallery by 27 February. There is no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery's door, no restriction on when the work was made, and no requirement that work be for sale - the gallery keeps 30% on anything sold and artists pay shipping both ways. Manifest runs its own darkroom and photo lab and publishes the INPHA photography annual, so photographic work sits squarely inside this call. The entry form takes up to twelve works at $10 each, paid by credit card via PayPal on the page that follows the form, or by US check or money order. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $10 per work. Prize: $50 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury.

item.title: Regional Showcase: Ohio, Kentucky & Indiana · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest's annual exhibit devoted to artists living in its own three-state region, a series the Cincinnati gallery launched thirteen years ago. "It is VERY important to note that this is NOT a call for works ABOUT Ohio, Kentucky, or Indiana. There is no thematic or media requirement. The exhibit is solely focused on works by artists living in the three states, to celebrate the diversity and quality of the artwork made by people in our region." The only limitation is residence: entries must be original works made by artists currently living in Ohio, Kentucky or Indiana. Submissions "can range from the most traditional to the most conceptual or experimental", across any 2D, 3D or experimental medium, with no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery's door and no restriction on when the work was made - Manifest states it does "not believe great art has an expiration date". Selection is two-part: an anonymous several-member panel of professional and academic advisors scores the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibit curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium with no strings attached, and one work in each of the season's nine exhibition periods takes a $1,000 Grand Jury Award decided by a second-round jury of the top-scoring works. The exhibition runs 5 March - 2 April 2027; notifications are emailed to all entrants by 25 January 2027 and accepted work is due at the gallery by 27 February. Manifest is a 501(c)(3) run by artists for artists, with its own darkroom and photo lab and an international photography annual, and it notes that the entry fee "is the only cost charged by Manifest for participation" - though artists pay shipping both ways and the gallery keeps 30% on work that sells. The entry form takes up to twelve works: $45 covers the first three, then $5 each. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 works) + $5 each. Prize: $50 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury.

item.title: Juried Artist Membership 2026 · Rockport Art Association & Museum
item.description: Once a year the Rockport Art Association & Museum - founded in 1921 on Cape Ann, with galleries at 12 Main Street - juries new Juried Artist Members, and Photography is one of its four standing categories alongside Painting, Graphics and Sculpture. Admission is by merit: "Juried Artist Members ... are admitted through an annual jury process in the fall that evaluates the merit of their work based on professionalism of technique and originality." Applicants submit five original works in one category, created solely by the applicant - no work made in classes or under supervision - framed or presented to a professional standard, and the actual physical works must be delivered to the museum for the jury to see (drop-off Tuesday 27 October, pick-up Thursday 29 October). Photographs may not be printed smaller than 11 by 14 inches and frames may not exceed 20 by 24 inches at the opening. The jury votes silently and a photography applicant needs at least four of five votes in favour; works that split 60/40 are reviewed a second time, when a juror may speak for or against. No feedback is given. The RAA&M states there is no longer a New England residency requirement to apply. Accepted artists have about two works chosen for the New Juried Artist Members Show, 7-29 November 2026, with a reception on 7 November, and membership then brings "exhibition opportunities in solo, member group, non-juried & juried shows; opportunities to instruct and attend workshops; and participation in year-round classes, sketch groups, lectures and artist demonstrations". The application fee is $50 whatever the category - you may apply in more than one category on a single fee, but must submit five works per category - and it is deducted from the $150 annual dues if you are accepted. The association insures nothing: "The RAA&M does not offer insurance on works submitted by applicants." — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: $50 ($150 dues if accepted). Prize: Juried artist membership + group exhibition.

item.title: Earth Photo 2027
item.description: Earth Photo is the free international platform for photographers and filmmakers who work on the natural world, its peoples and environments: "From the effects of climate change and biodiversity loss to powerful acts of restoration, resilience and hope, Earth Photo sheds light on the stories behind the images." Established in 2018 by Parker Harris with the Royal Geographical Society and Forestry England, and organised in partnership with Photoworks, it is open to artists and image-makers worldwide working in any lens-based media. Each entrant may submit up to ten works, still or moving - short films between five seconds and five minutes - with a CV up to 500 words, a 100-word artist statement and a caption or statement for each work. Work should have been made in the last five years, though earlier images may be included as part of a long-term documentary project, archive or vernacular series. The Earth Photo team longlists the most compelling submissions for a jury of industry experts chaired by Louise Fedotov-Clements, Director of Photoworks, with the shortlist then considered for exhibition and awards; final decisions rest with the Earth Photo team and its exhibition and award partners. The awards are substantial and various: the Earth Photo Award 2027 (£1,000), the Climate of Change Award (£500), the Moving Image Award (£500), a two-week Sidney Nolan Trust residency at The Rodd with access to Nolan's photographic archives for a UK-based practitioner, two David Wolf Kaye Future Potential Awards of £1,000 plus mentoring for practitioners aged 25 or under, a £400 Photoworks digital residency, mentoring from the New Scientist editorial team with a possible feature in its Aperture section, and a QUAD feature exhibition. Shortlisted and winning work opens at the Royal Geographical Society in London on 5 July 2027 and then tours UK venues - the 2026 edition travelled to National Trust properties, Belvoir Castle, Chester Zoo, Heligan Gardens and Castle Ward among others - with publication in the RGS magazine Geographical and RGS membership for the award winners. The cutoff is not end of day: the KEY DATES block reads "Online submission deadline 3 February 2027, 5pm GMT". Entrants are notified on 11 March 2027; high-res files are due 25 March. — Deadline: February 3, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 + exhibitions + residency.

item.title: GOING GREEN · MVA Gallery
item.description: A national call from the MVA Gallery in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, built entirely around one colour: "Green is located in the center of the color spectrum as if to proclaim its significance as the center of the color universe!" The gallery asks how you use it - "Does the color permeate your entire image or is it used in small sections? Does it appear in your artwork in objects or in nature or in portrait studies or in abstract design? Is Green purely decorative, or is it a narrative or structural device?" - and sets no other limit: "No restrictions on subject matter or style exist for this exhibition. All approaches are acceptable - traditional or experimental, representational or abstract, unified or fragmented, lucid or mysterious." Photography is a named medium and the prospectus is unusually welcoming about process and presentation: "All photographic processes are welcome", with framing in black or white preferred for a traditional presentation, white or off-white mats, and unframed mounting considered. There is no cutoff date for when the work was made. A small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers, curators and academics juries the entries and has requested anonymity for this show; decisions are final and no feedback is given. Awards are an "Art of Distinction" award - a featured solo presentation in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date - a $200 Director's Choice award at the Executive Director's discretion, honourable mentions that carry free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity chosen in December from everyone exhibited that calendar year. The exhibition runs 4-28 April 2027; artists are notified on or about 11 February 2027 and accepted work must reach the gallery by 31 March. Work has to arrive ready to hang with stretched wire on the back, under 48 inches framed and 45 lbs, plexiglass preferred over glass; artists pay shipping and insurance both ways and must enclose a prepaid return label. The gallery keeps 30% on sales. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: BBA One Shot Award - Winter 2027
item.description: BBA Gallery's single-image prize, the Berlin gallery's most accessible open call: "We are looking for that one definitive frame that stops viewers in their tracks." One photograph, one €19 entry, and the gallery's own summary of the rules is "1 shot - 0 rules (almost)" - "You do not need a massive portfolio or an expensive series to make an impact in the art world", "We welcome artists of any background, nationality, and ability, our only rule is that you must be over 18 to apply", and "You can submit work in absolutely any photographic medium or genre." A shortlist of 20 images is professionally printed and hung at BBA Gallery with all production costs covered by the gallery, and a longlist of 50 is shown on a large digital display in the space; there is no shipping cost to the artist. First prize is €300 in cash plus the exhibition, an Artsy profile and promotion through the gallery's social channels and newsletter, and selected images are also featured weekly online as Shot of the Week. BBA runs these prizes as an entry point into its gallery programme rather than as a one-off: "We built these open calls not just to hand out titles, but to foster real connections between emerging talent and the established art world", and it says prize artists go on to its Berlin events, group shows, art-fair representation and solo exhibitions. Previous One Shot winners include Michael Bulgrin (Germany), Rik Roos and Peter Alfred Hamelinck (Netherlands), Pervin Donmez (Latvia) and Calogero Cammalleri (Italy). Two conditions sit in the terms rather than the pitch: submitted work "must be available exclusive for sale throughout the exhibition and three months after if sales are made through BBA Gallery", and the gallery takes 50% commission on anything it sells. Entry is one .jpg, .png or .heic file up to 3 MB, uploaded after the fee is paid. — Deadline: February 22, 2027. Fee: €19. Prize: €300 + Berlin exhibition.

item.title: smallworks 2026
item.description: ROY G BIV's annual small-format holiday show, open to the Columbus nonprofit's own Artist and ROY Alumni members. Every piece must fit inside a 12 x 12 x 12 inch envelope — two-dimensional work included, so photography and lens-based work qualify as long as it arrives ready to hang with the right hardware. You can submit up to five entries and the gallery guarantees each member at least one accepted work, with a maximum of three, which makes this one of the rare juried shows where entering is close to a certainty of being hung. The gallery asks artists to price work 'in the spirit of the season of giving' and splits any sale 65% to the artist, 35% to ROY. Submission is by email with the subject 'smallworks 2026': attach high-quality JPEG or PNG images named only with a number, each no larger than 1.5 MB and never zipped, plus a list of works giving title, date, media, size and price; submissions missing the artist's full name, mailing address, attached images or attached list of works will not be considered. Artists are notified of admittance on Sunday November 15, accepted work is delivered to the gallery at 435 West Rich Street on Saturday November 28 and Sunday November 29 between 12:30 and 5:30pm EST, and the artist is responsible for transport both ways. The gallery states on its mission page that the price of work shown at ROY includes its 35% commission, reinvested in the gallery. ROY G BIV has run for 37 years and given over 1,000 emerging artists their exhibiting opportunity; its alumni hold work in permanent collections at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney, MoMA PS1, the Louvre, the Getty, Tate Modern and the Columbus Museum of Art, and hold "64 major awards (that we know of), including 2 Guggenheim Fellows". Membership in the Artist or Alumni tier is the only cost, taken through the gallery's Donorbox form, which publishes no fixed price. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: PWYC. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Best of the Beach
item.description: A juried show at Gallery of Hermosa on Pier Avenue in Hermosa Beach, presented with the local Easy Reader newspaper, and the gallery is blunt that this is not a beach-art show: 'Artistic excellence is the standard, and there is no required subject. Subject matter, style, and medium are open.' The title is meant as an invitation rather than a theme — submit the work you believe is your best and say why it belongs. A short artist statement of up to 100 words is strongly recommended with each entry, and the gallery offers several readings to work from: your strongest piece, the beach as literal subject (coastline, water, light, wildlife, surf culture, life by the sea), the beach as metaphor (shoreline, tide, horizon, edge, impermanence, the meeting of two worlds), a personal connection to a place or community, or your own take. Open to local, national and international artists in any medium: 2D work in all media plus smaller 3D sculpture. Best in Show takes $500 and an article in Easy Reader, whose length, format and timing the paper decides; second place takes $200, third $100, and four further awards $50 each, announced at the opening reception, where winners need not be present. Entry is $36 for up to three images, with detail shots counting toward that total, and the jury's decision does not guarantee acceptance. Decisions are emailed November 30, accepted work is dropped off December 7–9, the reception runs Saturday December 12 from 2 to 5pm, and the exhibition hangs December 12, 2026 to January 10, 2027, with pick-up on January 11–12. All accepted work must be offered for sale, at the gallery and online, from the time of acceptance — work marked not for sale is not eligible — and neither the gallery nor the CaFE prospectus states a commission on a sale. The artist is responsible for delivering or shipping work to and from the gallery. Two-dimensional work may be up to 48 inches wide by 72 inches high including the frame and 25 lbs, must arrive ready to hang on braided picture wire (no sawtooth hangers), and anything over 20 inches on a side must be glazed with acrylic rather than glass; photographs must be framed or mounted on board, and must be unique or part of a limited edition, with the series and edition noted on the work. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $36 for up to 3 images. Prize: $500 + Easy Reader article / $200 / $100 + 4×$50.

item.title: THROWING SHADE · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's online juried exhibit on light and shadow — the organisers write that the two 'speak to the parts of us that words miss', light revealing and shadow concealing, and that in the space between them mystery and emotion come alive. They want your version of that in any medium. Open worldwide to amateur and professional artists in all fine art media, with photography named explicitly in the list alongside oil, acrylic, watermedia, pastel, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, fiber, wood, ceramics, film/video and digital art; AI will not be accepted, work previously selected for an Art Fluent exhibit is not eligible, and neither is work copied or made under an instructor's guidance. Curated and juried by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill with an anonymous committee of jurors — there is no personal feedback. Best of Show takes $750 and two Director's Choice awards take $250 each; every accepted piece is shown in the online gallery at art-fluent.com, sales enquiries go straight to the artist and the artist keeps 100% of any sale. JPEGs are due by midnight MST on Friday, January 8, 2027, with notification and the online gallery opening by February 5. Entry is $25 for the first piece and $10 for each additional, up to twenty in total; diptychs and triptychs upload as a single image, and a portion of the entry-fee proceeds is donated to arts organisations. — Deadline: January 8, 2027. Fee: $25 + $10 each additional. Prize: $750 + 2×$250.

item.title: FRAME/SEQUENCE Issue 4 — On the Destruction of Art
item.description: FRAME/SEQUENCE is a Philadelphia print periodical founded in 2025 by photographer and educator Lily Colman (RISD MFA, 2020) as a publishing non-profit under the fiscal sponsorship of CultureWorks of Philadelphia, spotlighting underrepresented and emerging photographers, writers, artists and communities across Philadelphia and Greater Pennsylvania. Issue 4, due out as the March 2027 periodical, takes the theme "On the Destruction of Art": what it means to make work in an age of cultural and societal destruction, how artists keep working in those conditions, and how a society responds when art itself is debased, degraded or commodified. The editors want work that uses destruction or ephemerality as method — rupture and renewal — alongside writing that reads art's place in culture through an art-historical or contemporary lens, and they say explicitly that they are looking for everything from photographers working on the ground in real time to more interpretive photographic and written responses. The regional frame is relaxed for this issue: the periodical still focuses on Philadelphia, but submissions for Issue 4 are open to any artist or writer, and former University of the Arts students forced to transfer when that school closed, along with their professors, are especially encouraged. Photography, creative writing (poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction), visual art, mixed media and community-focused projects are accepted, and all visual art must incorporate photography in some way. Submit between five and ten images per edition as JPEG or PNG through the Airtable form, each file under 10 MB, 240 dpi acceptable and 300 dpi preferred for print; previously published work is eligible as long as you retain the right to republish, noted in the submission. There is no submission fee: the FAQ on the Issue 4 call page states "There is no submission fee. FRAME/SEQUENCE believes in removing financial barriers to participation in the arts community." Accepted contributors are paid a one-time cash award per accepted piece plus a royalty apportioned by level of contribution out of a shared royalty pool paid through the fiscal sponsor; artists keep full ownership and all rights and may keep using, selling or publishing the work, signing a publishing agreement by DocuSign if selected. Three inconsistencies sit on the organiser's own pages, and one of them is about money. The submissions FAQ still answers the deadline question with the inaugural issue's window (June 20 – July 18, 2025), while the dated Issue 4 block on both the submissions page and the homepage reads September 15 – November 15, 2026. The About page says twice that the periodical charges nothing to submit — "we do not charge a submission fee, and we pay our artists for having their work published" and "submissions are always free" — the live Issue 4 Airtable form carries no payment step, no fee line and no membership question, and as of 13 October 2026 the call page's own FAQ agrees: "There is no submission fee." And the team page calls the periodical quarterly where the homepage and submissions page call it semiannual. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + cash award per accepted piece.
